title: Probability and random processes
description: Probability models, distributions, conditioning, transformations, and stochastic reasoning.
guidance: Define the sample space, event, random variable, support, and assumptions before choosing a formula.
Distinguish independence from mutual exclusivity and conditional probability from joint probability.
For every distribution include parameters, support, PMF or PDF, CDF, mean, variance, and when the model applies.
Use probability_distribution or math_binomial for supported distributions and embed the returned chart artifact.
Distinguish probability density from point probability; continuous random variables have zero point mass.
For transformations, derive the valid domain, inverse branches, and absolute Jacobian before substitution.
For joint distributions, verify normalization and derive marginals before assuming independence.
State convergence and approximation assumptions for limit theorems; distinguish random variables from sample paths.
Label created practice questions as original and use actual uploaded tutorial citations for sourced questions.
